headline: Who owns the water: Bengaluru's allocation ledger
intro: Bengaluru drinks under the most litigated water instrument in India: the Cauvery award. A tribunal first earmarked the city just 1.75 TMC a year - reasoning that only a third of it lies in the basin - and it took the Supreme Court until 2018 to nearly quadruple that. This ledger shows what the paper now promises, what Karnataka has allocated to its water board, what the pumps actually deliver, and where the record goes quiet.
unit_note: Inter-state entitlements are in TMC per year (1 TMC is about 28.3 billion litres; 10 TMC/yr is roughly 775 MLD - BWSSB's own conversion). Pumping capacities are in MLD. The interstate earmark (consumptive) and Karnataka's gross drawal allocation are different accounting bases - both are shown, never mixed.

authorities.name: Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA / CWRC)
authorities.role: The central bodies created after the 2018 judgment to regulate Cauvery releases between the states, month by month. When reservoirs run low, Bengaluru's drinking share is argued out here.
authorities.tension: In June 2026, with reservoir levels declining, BWSSB asked the regulation committee to reserve 9.56 TMC exclusively for drinking water - the entitlement on paper still has to be won operationally every dry year.

authorities.name: Government of Karnataka (Urban Development Dept)
authorities.role: Allocates BWSSB's share out of Karnataka's 284.75 TMC. The original 19 TMC was fully committed by 2012; a further 10 TMC (775 MLD) was carved out of irrigation use for Stage V by a Principal Secretary's letter in January 2014.
authorities.tension: The letter that allocated Bengaluru's newest 10 TMC has never been published - it is known only because a Japanese aid appraisal quoted it.

entitled.basis: CWDT 2007 award (1.75) + Supreme Court 2018 addition (4.75), consumptive
entitled.note: The tribunal assumed a third of the city is in-basin and half its need would come from groundwater; the Supreme Court rejected both assumptions, citing the city's growth

received.note: No public year-wise drawal-in-TMC series exists against the earmark - a named gap

instrument.label: CWDT Final Award (5 Feb 2007, gazetted 2013) + Supreme Court judgment (16 Feb 2018)

arrangements.note: Karnataka's overall share rose from 270 to 284.75 TMC in the same judgment.

entitled.basis: gross drawal: 19 TMC original allocation + 10 TMC (775 MLD) added by UDD letter, 27 Jan 2014

received.note: Delivery runs ~1,500 MLD against ~2,293 MLD installed across six pumping stages - Stage V (775 MLD, commissioned Oct 2024) was delivering roughly 400 MLD by mid-2026 as connections ramp

instrument.label: BWSSB official statement (19 + 10 TMC) + JICA Phase-3 appraisal (letter date)

arrangements.note: Gross drawal vs the 6.5 TMC consumptive earmark above - different accounting bases, both official.

events.title: CWDT final award: Bengaluru gets 1.75 TMC
events.note: The tribunal earmarks just 1.75 TMC for the city's domestic and industrial use, assuming half its drinking need would come from groundwater. Gazetted only in 2013.

events.title: Karnataka carves 10 TMC out of irrigation for Stage V
events.note: A Principal Secretary (UDD) letter of 27 January 2014 allocates a further 10 TMC (775 MLD) to BWSSB - the paper behind Cauvery Stage V. The letter itself has never been published.

events.title: Supreme Court nearly quadruples the city's earmark
events.note: The 16 February 2018 judgment adds 4.75 TMC for Bengaluru's drinking water (to ~6.5 TMC consumptive), explicitly rejecting the tribunal's one-third-basin and groundwater assumptions. The CWMA and CWRC are constituted months later to police releases.

events.title: Cauvery Stage V commissioned (775 MLD)
events.note: Commissioned 16 October 2024, taking installed pumping to ~2,293 MLD across six stages - the 2014 letter's water finally arrives in the city's pipes.

futures.status: Karnataka's proposed balancing reservoir on the Cauvery, pitched substantially as Bengaluru drinking-water storage; opposed by Tamil Nadu and without central clearances - the next chapter of the award fight

gaps: No public year-wise series of BWSSB's actual drawal in TMC against its ~29 TMC permission - CWRC/CWMA minutes or an RTI are the likely routes.
The UDD letter of 27 Jan 2014 (the instrument behind Stage V's 10 TMC) is not public; it is known only via a JICA appraisal.
Installed-capacity figures vary by source (stage components sum to 2,085 MLD; the board's chairman says 2,293; press repeats 2,225) - this ledger uses the chairman's figure with the conflict noted.
No audited post-Stage-V delivered-MLD figure exists yet; ~1,500 MLD is corroborated press.
